summary.headline: Q1 FY27 profit described as second highest in company history after Q1 FY22, driven by better realisations despite lower sales volumes.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 was shaped by Middle East war escalation and de-escalation, which caused viability-driven shutdowns at acetic acid, ethyl acetate and TDI but lifted realisations. Sales volumes fell well below production, and inventory built up to 30 June was about 15% liquidated by end-July. Fertilizer segment profit rose to about INR85 crores from about INR24 crores, with urea contributing about INR48 crores and ANP about INR12 crores. Management gave no formal quarterly guidance, and several questions on forward realisations and savings went unanswered.

financial_highlights.value: Second highest in company history after Q1 FY22

financial_highlights.change: Up about INR60 crores from about INR24 crores
Held across G-Sec, GSFS and bank

segments.name: Fertilizers (urea, ANP)
segments.commentary: Fertilizer segment result rose to about INR85 crores from about INR24 crores, with urea about INR48 crores and ANP about INR12 crores. Energy norm for urea revised to 6.37 Gcal/MT from 6.20 Gcal/MT, valid for 3 years from FY26.

segments.name: Chemicals (TDI, WNA, CNA, AN Melt, TGU, acetic acid, ethyl acetate)
segments.commentary: Q1 output: TDI 12,800 MT, WNA 113,000 MT (sales 20,800 MT), CNA production 37,500 MT (sales 16,400 MT), AN Melt 55,600 MT, TGU 74,800 MT, formic acid 8,200 MT. Acetic acid and ethyl acetate were shut for part of the quarter; both restarted by 1 August.

guidance_outlook: Management expects TGU output for the rest of FY27 to be broadly at last year's level, against a Q1 run rate it described as about 300,000 MT annualised.

Steam portion of the coal-based Dahej steam and power project is running; power expected in about 45 days. Estimated saving of INR30,000-40,000 per MT of TDI at current gas and coal prices, subject to change.

A.T. Kearney cost-saving quantification is not yet signed off; management expects a clearer P&L picture by end of Q2. Earlier Kearney estimate cited by an analyst was INR250-300 crores, which management confirmed.
Projected incremental revenue of INR1,200-1,500 crores and contribution uplift of INR500-600 crores from the INR2,800 crore project portfolio, given later and subject to price volatility.

Capex for FY27 targeted at INR1,200-1,500 crores more on top of Q1 INR300 crores; most will sit in CWIP, with only partial capitalisation in FY27. Remaining projects commercially operational around mid-2027. Further about INR1,500 crores over the next two years.
capex_capacity: Dahej CCPP (INR613 crores) and other projects are targeted for commercial operation around mid-2027.
Dahej steam portion is online and replacing gas with coal for TDI-II; power portion expected in roughly 45 days.
Weak nitric acid plant running about 3 months behind schedule, to be recouped; AMUGL and AN Melt reported online.
Ammonia output about 173,000 MT, split 54% oil-based and 49% gas-based (as stated, shares sum above 100%). TDI output split 66% Dahej and 34% Bharuch.

Urea and nitric acid ran above rated capacity; CNA ran below design capacity due to weak internal TDI consumption; aniline and nitrobenzene ran above design. Minimum neem coated urea obligation is 637,000 MT.
demand_pricing: TDI: management said global TDI supply exceeds demand, so Covestro and Wanhua maintenance shutdowns will not move global pricing, though Indian TDI shortage will affect local pricing.
Inventory built to 30 June was about 15% liquidated by end-July; realisations were initially lower, then rose, with no single figure given.
Offtake was weak in Q1 even though spreads looked better, causing inventory build-up.
Management declined to give Q2 vs Q1 realisation direction, citing market volatility.
Fuel oil and gas prices rose versus Q4 FY26 on the Middle East crisis; oil prices (per analyst) moved from about INR43-44 to about INR73; easing seen in July-August but not resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Current oil and gas prices and availability versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: N.B. Desai said prices eased in July-August but the Middle East crisis is unresolved; gas prices are volatile, though supply has not affected operations.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 realisation direction for chemicals vs Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing that Q1 was the reference point and the market is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej steam and power savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about INR30,000-40,000 per MT of TDI; the figure moves with the gas-coal price delta, and coal-based operation benefits if coal prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Cash, capex and project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash about INR4,000 crores; Q1 capex INR300 crores; FY27 capex targeted at INR1,200-1,500 crores more; INR2,800 crore projects on hand plus about INR1,500 crores over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Plant restart status for acetic acid, ethyl acetate and TDI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethyl acetate and acetic acid back on 1 August after July and May shutdowns; Bharuch TDI was down in July, with TDI-I and TDI-II restarting. Methanol sourcing for captive acetic acid has started.

risks_watch: Re-escalation of the Middle East conflict could reopen viability issues and shut plants again, as seen in Q1.
Unsigned Kearney savings estimate; the INR250-300 crore planned saving has not been confirmed by management.
Inventory liquidation and realisation mix in Q2 are unclear; offtake was weak in Q1.
Project timelines: Dahej CCPP and other projects slated for mid-2027; nitric acid plant about 3 months behind.
Gas and coal price volatility drives the Dahej steam and power savings and TDI economics.
Management declined to quantify several forward items (Q2 realisations, project revenue impact), limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q1 profitability and project progress, but evasive on forward realisations, guidance and project revenue, repeatedly citing volatility and avoiding numbers.
